sides.text: Linear and time-invariant: predictable input-to-output behavior

more.text: Superposition holds and delaying the input just delays the output. An LTI system is fully described by its impulse response h(t), and the output is the input convolved with h.

sides.text: A system's response to a delayed input is just the delayed response. Which property is that?

more.text: Time invariance.
Slide the flipped impulse response across the input and integrate. In the frequency domain, convolution becomes multiplication.

sides.text: What does convolution in time become in the frequency domain?

more.text: Multiplication.

sides.text: Periodic signals as sums of harmonics

more.text: x(t) = Σ cₙ e^(j2πnf₀t). An ideal square wave has only odd harmonics, with amplitudes falling as 1/n.

sides.text: Which harmonics does an ideal square wave contain, and how do their amplitudes scale?

more.text: The odd harmonics, falling as 1/n.
X(f) = ∫ x(t) e^(−j2πft) dt. A time shift adds phase. Compressing a signal in time stretches its spectrum.

sides.text: A very narrow pulse in time has what kind of spectrum?

more.text: A wide one.

sides.text: Generalizes Fourier using s = σ + jω

more.text: It turns differential equations into algebra. Poles and zeros of the resulting transfer function describe a system's behavior.

sides.text: What does the Laplace transform do to a linear differential equation?

more.text: Turns it into an algebraic equation in s.

sides.text: H(s) = output / input in the s-domain

more.text: Poles (roots of the denominator) set stability and speed; zeros shape the response. A first-order low-pass is H(s) = 1 / (1 + sRC).

sides.text: H(s) = 1 / (1 + sRC). Where is the pole?

more.text: At s = −1/(RC), the cutoff angular frequency.
A pole with a positive real part grows exponentially. Poles on the jω axis oscillate indefinitely.

sides.text: A system has a pole at s = +2. Is it stable?

more.text: No. It grows like e^(2t).

sides.text: Natural frequency ωₙ and damping ζ set the response

more.text: ζ < 1 overshoots (underdamped), ζ = 1 is critically damped, ζ > 1 is overdamped. Overshoot ≈ e^(−πζ/√(1−ζ²)).

sides.text: ζ = 0.5. What is the approximate step overshoot?

more.text: About 16%.
The step shows rise time, overshoot, and settling. The impulse response h(t) fully characterizes an LTI system.

sides.text: Which response fully characterizes an LTI system?

more.text: The impulse response.

sides.text: Each pole adds −20 dB/decade; each zero adds +20

more.text: Straight-line approximations let you sketch a frequency response by hand.

sides.text: A response has two poles beyond the cutoff. What is the slope?

more.text: −40 dB/decade.

sides.text: High frequencies masquerade as low ones

more.text: A tone at f sampled at fs appears at |f − k·fs| closest to the baseband. Filter before sampling.

sides.text: A 7 kHz tone is sampled at 10 kHz. At what frequency does it appear?

more.text: 3 kHz.
Bin spacing is fs / N. Bin k represents frequency k × fs / N.

sides.text: fs = 48 kHz and N = 1,024. What is the bin spacing?

more.text: About 46.9 Hz.

sides.text: Computes the DFT in O(N log N)

more.text: Cooley–Tukey splits a size-N transform into two size-N/2 transforms and combines them with butterflies.

sides.text: For N = 1,024, about how many times fewer operations does the FFT need than a direct DFT?

more.text: About 100 times fewer (N² vs N log₂ N).
A signal that doesn't fit a whole number of cycles in the window smears energy across bins. Hann and Hamming windows reduce leakage at the cost of a wider main lobe.

sides.text: An FFT of a pure tone shows energy spread across many bins. What's the likely cause?

more.text: Spectral leakage. Apply a window.
A digital filter is stable if all its poles lie inside the unit circle.

sides.text: Where must a stable digital filter's poles lie?

more.text: Inside the unit circle.
Always stable, and can have exactly linear phase. Needs more taps than an IIR filter for a sharp cutoff.

sides.text: A 5-tap moving average with equal coefficients of 1/5. What is its DC gain?

more.text: More efficient for a given sharpness, but can be unstable and has nonlinear phase. Often designed from analog filters with the bilinear transform.

sides.text: Which digital filter type can become unstable?

more.text: IIR.
Low-pass filter before decimating to prevent aliasing; filter after interpolating to remove images.
To prevent aliasing.

sides.text: Maximizes SNR for a known pulse

more.text: The filter's impulse response is a time-reversed copy of the signal. Equivalent to correlating with the expected waveform.

sides.text: What does a matched filter maximize?

more.text: Output signal-to-noise ratio for a known pulse.
White noise has a flat PSD. Integrating the PSD over a band gives the power in that band.

sides.text: What is the PSD of ideal white noise?

more.text: Flat across frequency.
Small signals sit on a DC operating point. A BJT's gm = Ic / V_T, where V_T is about 25.9 mV at 300 K.

sides.text: A BJT is biased at Ic = 1 mA. What is gm?

more.text: About 38.7 mS.
Common-emitter: high gain, inverts. Common-collector (emitter follower): gain near 1, low output impedance. Common-base: good at high frequency, low input impedance.

sides.text: Which BJT stage is a buffer with gain near 1?

more.text: The common-collector (emitter follower).
In square-law operation, transconductance rises with drain current. Common-source stage gain is −gm × Rd.

sides.text: Id = 1 mA and an overdrive voltage of 0.2 V. What is gm?

more.text: 10 mS.
C_in ≈ C_gd × (1 + |A|). It lowers bandwidth in inverting amplifiers. A cascode stage reduces it.

sides.text: C_gd = 2 pF and gain = −50. What is the Miller capacitance?

more.text: About 102 pF.
Raises output resistance and bandwidth by shielding the input transistor from large voltage swing, reducing the Miller effect.

sides.text: What problem does a cascode stage reduce?

more.text: The Miller effect (and it raises output resistance).

sides.text: Amplifies the difference between two inputs

more.text: A tail current source splits between two transistors. It rejects common-mode signals and is the input stage of nearly every op-amp.

sides.text: What signals does a differential pair reject?

more.text: Common-mode signals.

sides.text: Copies one current to another branch

more.text: A diode-connected transistor sets the reference current and a matched transistor reproduces it. Used for biasing and active loads.

sides.text: What sets the output current of a current mirror?

more.text: The reference current through the diode-connected transistor.
Gain-bandwidth product is roughly constant in a voltage-feedback op-amp.

sides.text: GBW = 1 MHz and a closed-loop gain of 20. What is the bandwidth?

more.text: About 50 kHz.

sides.text: The maximum rate of output change

more.text: To pass a full-amplitude sine without distortion: SR ≥ 2π f Vp.

sides.text: 10 V peak at 100 kHz. What minimum slew rate is needed?

more.text: About 6.3 V/µs.

sides.text: Input offset voltage and bias current

more.text: They produce an output error that grows with gain. Matching source resistances and using precision parts reduce it.

sides.text: What produces a DC error at an op-amp's output even with zero input?

more.text: Input offset voltage and bias currents.

sides.text: Rejection of common-mode and supply noise

more.text: CMRR = differential gain / common-mode gain, in dB. PSRR measures how well supply ripple is rejected.

sides.text: What does a high CMRR mean?

more.text: The amplifier strongly rejects common-mode signals.
Feedback trades gain for stability, linearity, bandwidth, and predictable gain (about 1/β when Aβ is large).

sides.text: With high loop gain, what mostly sets the closed-loop gain?

more.text: The feedback network (about 1/β).

sides.text: How far from instability a feedback loop is

more.text: The distance from −180° at the frequency where loop gain is 1 (0 dB). About 45° or more is a common target; low margin means ringing.

sides.text: What does a low phase margin cause in a step response?

more.text: Ringing and overshoot.
Sallen–Key is a common second-order stage. Butterworth: maximally flat. Chebyshev: steeper but with ripple. Bessel: best step response and linear phase.

sides.text: Which filter response is maximally flat in the passband?

more.text: Butterworth.
Each added order adds one pole and 20 dB/decade of attenuation.

sides.text: What is the roll-off of a 4th-order Butterworth filter?

more.text: −80 dB/decade.
Sustained oscillation needs a loop gain of exactly 1 and a total phase shift of 0° (or 360°). Types: Wien bridge, RC phase shift, LC (Colpitts, Hartley), crystal.

sides.text: What two conditions does the Barkhausen criterion set?

more.text: Loop gain of 1 and loop phase of 0° (or 360°).

sides.text: Locks an oscillator to a reference

more.text: A phase detector, loop filter, and VCO. Used for clock multiplication, frequency synthesis, and demodulation.

sides.text: Which block in a PLL sets the output frequency?

more.text: The voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO).
Flash is fastest but costly. SAR is a common mid-speed choice. Pipeline is fast with high resolution. Delta-sigma gives high resolution at lower speeds.

sides.text: Which ADC type gives the highest resolution at lower speeds?

more.text: Delta-sigma.

sides.text: A binary search for the input voltage

more.text: Compares the input against a DAC output, bit by bit from the MSB, so an N-bit conversion takes N cycles.

sides.text: How many comparison cycles does a 12-bit SAR ADC need?

more.text: A fast 1-bit quantizer pushes noise to high frequency, where a digital filter removes it. Excellent for audio and precision sensors.

sides.text: What two techniques give a delta-sigma converter its resolution?

more.text: Oversampling and noise shaping.
R-2R needs only two resistor values, which makes matching easier than binary-weighted resistors.

sides.text: Which DAC uses only two resistor values?

more.text: The R-2R ladder.
Class A: linear, inefficient. Class B: push-pull, at most 78.5% efficient, with crossover distortion. Class AB: small bias removes crossover. Class D: switching, over 90%.

sides.text: What is the maximum theoretical efficiency of a class B amplifier?

more.text: Thermal (Johnson) noise comes from resistors. Shot noise comes from discrete charge crossing a barrier. Flicker (1/f) noise dominates at low frequency.

sides.text: Which noise rises toward low frequencies?

more.text: Flicker (1/f) noise.

sides.text: How much a stage degrades SNR

more.text: NF = 10 log₁₀(SNR_in / SNR_out). In a cascade, the first stage dominates (Friis formula), so a low-noise amplifier goes first.

sides.text: An amplifier has a 3 dB noise figure. How does it change the SNR?

more.text: It degrades SNR by 3 dB.

sides.text: Current always returns to its source

more.text: High-frequency return current follows the path of least impedance, usually directly under the trace. Ground loops pick up noise.

sides.text: Where does high-frequency return current flow on a PCB?

more.text: Directly beneath the signal trace, in the ground plane.

sides.text: Small capacitors close, larger ones nearby

more.text: Place 0.1 µF ceramics at each supply pin with a short loop, and a bulk capacitor per section. Lower loop inductance matters more than capacitance.

sides.text: What matters most for effective decoupling placement?

more.text: A short, low-inductance loop.
Reduced by spacing, a nearby ground plane, and guard traces. Faster edges cause more crosstalk.

sides.text: How can you reduce crosstalk between PCB traces?

more.text: More spacing, a ground plane, and guard traces.
Control emissions and immunity with filtering, shielding, grounding, and slower edges. In the US, FCC Part 15 limits unintentional radiators.

sides.text: What does EMC stand for and mean?

more.text: Electromagnetic compatibility: not disturbing others and not being disturbed.
Use controlled impedance, proper termination, and short stubs. Ringing and reflections come from mismatches.

sides.text: What causes ringing on a fast digital line?

more.text: Impedance mismatches causing reflections.

sides.text: Clamp discharges before they reach the chip

more.text: TVS diodes at connectors and series resistance protect inputs. Follow standards such as IEC 61000-4-2.

sides.text: What component commonly protects USB lines against ESD?

more.text: A TVS diode.
Open-loop control follows a command with no measurement. Feedback corrects for disturbances and parameter changes.

sides.text: Which control type corrects for disturbances?

more.text: Closed-loop (feedback) control.
P reacts to present error, I removes steady-state error, D damps change. Beware integral windup and noise amplified by D.

sides.text: What problem arises when the integral term keeps growing while the actuator is saturated?

more.text: Integral windup.
Increase Kp until sustained oscillation (the ultimate gain), then derive gains from it. Modern practice uses relay or model-based tuning.

sides.text: Which classic method tunes PID gains from the ultimate gain and period?

more.text: Ziegler–Nichols.
A system with integral action (type 1) has zero steady-state error to a step input.
Integral action.
Gain margin is how much gain can rise before instability. Phase margin is how much extra lag can be added.

sides.text: What do gain and phase margins measure?

more.text: How far a feedback system is from instability.
Root locus shows how closed-loop poles move as gain changes. The Nyquist criterion tests stability from the open-loop frequency response.

sides.text: Which tool shows closed-loop poles moving with gain?

more.text: The root locus.

sides.text: ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du

more.text: Handles multi-input multi-output systems. The poles are the eigenvalues of A.

sides.text: What are a state-space system's poles?

more.text: The eigenvalues of A.
The loop runs at a fixed sample period. Delays reduce phase margin, so sample fast enough (often 10 to 20 times the bandwidth).

sides.text: Why can slow sampling destabilize a digital controller?

more.text: The added delay reduces phase margin.

sides.text: Solve G·v = i for node voltages

more.text: Modified nodal analysis builds a matrix from conductances and sources. Nonlinear devices are handled by Newton–Raphson, and transients by numerical integration.

sides.text: What does SPICE solve at each iteration?

more.text: A matrix equation for node voltages (modified nodal analysis).
x₍ₙ₊₁₎ = xₙ − f(xₙ) / f′(xₙ). SPICE linearizes diodes and transistors at each step with it.

sides.text: Which method does SPICE use to handle a diode's nonlinearity?

more.text: Newton–Raphson iteration.
Backward Euler is very stable but damps oscillation. The trapezoidal rule is more accurate but can ring. Step size matters.

sides.text: Which method is more accurate, backward Euler or trapezoidal?

more.text: The trapezoidal rule.
Tracks the best path through a trellis of states for convolutional codes, keeping the best survivor into each state.

sides.text: What kind of codes does the Viterbi algorithm decode?

more.text: Convolutional codes.
Adjusts filter weights to reduce error. Used in echo cancellation and noise cancelling. The step size μ trades speed for stability.

sides.text: What does μ control in the LMS algorithm?

more.text: The adaptation speed (and stability).
Shift data through an LFSR or a lookup table. The receiver recomputes and compares the remainder.

sides.text: Which arithmetic does a CRC use?

more.text: Modulo-2 polynomial division.

sides.text: Trig functions with only shifts and adds

more.text: Rotates a vector by a series of fixed angles. Useful on hardware without a multiplier.
Shifts, adds, and a small lookup table.
A one-line low-pass filter. A smaller α smooths more but responds more slowly.

sides.text: Which α gives more smoothing, 0.1 or 0.5?

more.text: Wye: V_line = √3 × V_phase and line current equals phase current. Delta: line voltage equals phase voltage and I_line = √3 × I_phase. Total power P = √3 × V_L × I_L × cos φ.

sides.text: 400 V line, 10 A, and a power factor of 0.9. What is the three-phase real power?

more.text: Dividing by a base value makes transformer and line parameters comparable across voltage levels. Common in power system analysis.

sides.text: Why use per-unit values in power system studies?

more.text: They remove voltage-level scaling, simplifying calculations across transformers.
Core loss (hysteresis and eddy currents), copper loss, and leakage inductance cause voltage regulation and heating. Open-circuit and short-circuit tests find the parameters.

sides.text: Which loss in a transformer depends on the core's magnetic behavior?

more.text: Core loss (hysteresis and eddy currents).

sides.text: Rotor locked to the rotating field

more.text: Used in power-plant generators. The speed is set by frequency and pole count. Excitation controls reactive power.

sides.text: What fixes a synchronous generator's speed?

more.text: The grid frequency and the number of poles.
The rotor must lag the rotating field to induce current. Slip rises with load.

sides.text: Synchronous speed 1,800 rpm and rotor speed 1,750 rpm. What is the slip?

more.text: About 2.8%.

sides.text: Back EMF: E = k φ ω

more.text: Torque is proportional to current and flux. Speed control by armature voltage is simple, but brushes wear.

sides.text: What opposes the supply as a DC motor speeds up?

more.text: Back EMF.
V/f keeps flux constant by scaling voltage with frequency. Field-oriented control (FOC) independently controls torque and flux for fast, precise response.

sides.text: Which control method independently regulates torque and flux?

more.text: Field-oriented control (FOC).
Inductor ripple current falls with larger L or higher switching frequency.

sides.text: Vin = 12 V, Vout = 5 V, D = 0.417, f = 100 kHz, and L = 47 µH. What's the ripple?

more.text: About 0.62 A.

sides.text: CCM keeps inductor current above zero

more.text: In DCM the current falls to zero each cycle, so the voltage ratio depends on the load. CCM gives a predictable Vout = D × Vin in a buck.

sides.text: In which mode is a buck converter's output ratio set only by duty cycle?

more.text: Continuous conduction mode (CCM).
Buck steps down, boost steps up, buck-boost inverts or does either. Flyback and forward isolate with a transformer. Flyback is common below about 100 W.

sides.text: Which topology provides isolation at low power levels?

more.text: Flyback.

sides.text: A saturated core stops acting like an inductor

more.text: Peak current must stay below the rated saturation current, or inductance collapses and current spikes.

sides.text: What happens if peak inductor current exceeds its saturation rating?

more.text: Inductance collapses and current spikes.
Conduction loss is I² × Rds(on). Switching loss is roughly ½ V I (t_r + t_f) f, plus gate-charge loss. Faster edges cut switching loss but raise EMI.

sides.text: Which loss rises directly with switching frequency?

more.text: Switching loss.
In a half-bridge, both switches must never conduct together. A short dead time between turn-off and turn-on avoids a shorted supply.

sides.text: What does dead time prevent in a half-bridge?

more.text: Shoot-through, where both switches conduct at once.

sides.text: Replace the diode with a MOSFET

more.text: A switch has a lower voltage drop than a diode, which raises efficiency, especially at low output voltages.
Lower loss than a diode, so higher efficiency.
A PFC stage (often a boost) shapes input current to follow the voltage, improving power factor and meeting harmonic limits.

sides.text: What does a PFC stage improve?

more.text: Power factor, by shaping input current to follow the voltage.

sides.text: Faster, hotter, higher voltage than silicon

more.text: Silicon carbide and gallium nitride switch quickly with low loss, enabling smaller magnetics and higher efficiency. SiC suits high voltage; GaN suits fast, lower-voltage designs.

sides.text: Which materials enable smaller, more efficient fast-switching converters?

more.text: Wide-bandgap semiconductors such as SiC and GaN.
Common-mode chokes and X/Y capacitors filter conducted EMI. RC snubbers damp ringing across switches.

sides.text: What does an RC snubber do?

more.text: Damps voltage ringing across a switch.

sides.text: Protect, balance, and gauge a pack

more.text:
Monitors cell voltage, current, and temperature
balances cells
and estimates state of charge (coulomb counting plus voltage). Cuts off unsafe conditions

sides.text: Which function keeps cells in a series pack at similar voltages?

more.text: Cell balancing.
LFP (lithium iron phosphate): safer, longer cycle life, lower energy density. NMC (nickel manganese cobalt): higher energy density. Choice trades cost, safety, range, and life.

sides.text: Which has higher energy density, NMC or LFP?

more.text: NMC.

sides.text: SoC: how full. SoH: how worn

more.text: SoC is estimated from voltage and integrated current. SoH tracks capacity fade and internal resistance rise over cycles.

sides.text: What does state of health describe?

more.text: How much a battery has degraded compared with new.
Inductive loads draw reactive power. Capacitor banks and inverters supply it to hold voltage. Frequency reflects supply-demand balance.
The balance between generation and load.
Lower losses over very long lines and undersea cables, and no reactive power issues. Needs expensive converter stations at each end.

sides.text: Why is HVDC used for very long undersea links?

more.text: No reactive-power problems and lower losses over distance.

sides.text: Detect faults and isolate them quickly

more.text: Relays sense overcurrent or distance to a fault and trip breakers. Coordination makes the nearest device act first (selectivity).

sides.text: What does selectivity mean in protection?

more.text: Only the device nearest the fault trips.

sides.text: Inverters synchronize and shut down if the grid fails

more.text: Grid-tied inverters follow grid voltage and frequency and must stop feeding if the grid goes down, protecting line workers.

sides.text: Why must grid-tied inverters stop if the grid fails?

more.text: To prevent islanding and protect utility workers.
Grid batteries are rated for both. Round-trip efficiency is energy out divided by energy in. Pumped hydro still dominates total capacity.

sides.text: A battery stores 100 kWh and discharges at 50 kW. How long does a full discharge take?

more.text: 2 hours.
Nudge the operating voltage and keep moving in the direction that raises power. Simple and widely used in solar chargers.
The operating voltage, in the direction that increases power.

sides.text: The 32-bit core in most modern microcontrollers

more.text: Thumb-2 instructions, a nested vectored interrupt controller, and optional FPU. Families M0, M3, M4, M7, and up.

sides.text: Which core family powers most STM32 microcontrollers?

more.text: ARM Cortex-M.
Lower numbers mean higher priority. A higher-priority interrupt can preempt a lower one. Latency is a few tens of cycles.

sides.text: Can a higher-priority interrupt preempt a running ISR on Cortex-M?

more.text: Yes. The NVIC supports nesting.
A DMA controller copies between peripherals and memory (ADC buffers, SPI, UART), freeing the CPU and improving throughput.

sides.text: What does DMA free the CPU from?

more.text: Copying data between peripherals and memory.

sides.text: Multiplying a crystal to a fast core clock

more.text: A PLL scales an 8 MHz crystal up to a hundred MHz or more. Peripherals have their own dividers and clock gates.

sides.text: How does an MCU reach 100 MHz from an 8 MHz crystal?

more.text: Using a PLL to multiply the clock.
Clock gating, lower voltage, deep sleep with wake-on-interrupt, and avoiding busy-waiting cut average current by orders of magnitude.

sides.text: Why is busy-waiting bad on a battery device?

more.text: It keeps the CPU awake and wastes power.
A preemptive scheduler runs the highest-priority ready task. Tools: queues, semaphores, mutexes, and timers. FreeRTOS and Zephyr are common.

sides.text: Which task does a preemptive scheduler run?

more.text: The highest-priority ready task.

sides.text: A low-priority task blocks a high-priority one

more.text: Occurs when a low-priority task holds a lock the high-priority task needs and a medium task preempts it. Priority inheritance fixes it, as on the Mars Pathfinder.
Priority inheritance.
A mutex protects a shared resource (the owner unlocks it). A semaphore signals events or counts resources.

sides.text: Which is used to signal that an event happened?

more.text: A semaphore.

sides.text: Shared data between an ISR and main code

more.text: A multi-step update can be interrupted mid-way. Protect it by briefly disabling interrupts or using atomic operations.

sides.text: Why can shared variables between an ISR and main code corrupt?

more.text: The update isn't atomic and can be interrupted.
Guaranteed schedulable if utilization ≤ n(2^(1/n) − 1), about 69% for many tasks.

sides.text: What's the utilization bound for 3 tasks under rate-monotonic scheduling?

more.text: About 78%.

sides.text: Missing a deadline is failure vs degradation

more.text: Hard: airbags and pacemakers. Soft: video and audio, where a missed deadline just lowers quality.

sides.text: Which real-time class includes an airbag controller?

more.text: Hard real time.
Faster memory is smaller and costs more. Flash can have wait states at high clock speed, so caches or prefetch help.

sides.text: Why do fast MCUs add caches or prefetch for flash?

more.text: Flash is slower than the core, so it needs wait states otherwise.
Free to use and extend. Growing in microcontrollers, with chips from Espressif and others.

sides.text: What makes RISC-V different from Arm?

more.text: It's an open ISA that anyone can implement without licensing fees.
A bootloader verifies a signature on the next stage, forming a chain of trust. Protects against tampered firmware.
That the firmware is signed by a trusted key.
Use signed images, two partitions (A/B), and automatic rollback so a failed update doesn't brick the device.

sides.text: Why use A/B partitions for updates?

more.text: So a failed update can roll back.
A debug probe gives breakpoints, single-stepping, and memory inspection. Logic analyzers and printf logging cover timing and protocols.

sides.text: Which interface lets you set breakpoints on a Cortex-M?

more.text: SWD (or JTAG).
Messages have IDs, and lower IDs win arbitration. Classic CAN runs up to 1 Mbit/s and has built-in error handling.

sides.text: How does CAN decide which message goes first?

more.text: Arbitration by ID, where the lowest ID wins.
Devices expose endpoints and describe themselves with descriptors. Full speed is 12 Mbit/s, high speed 480 Mbit/s, and SuperSpeed 5 Gbit/s.

sides.text: What is the full-speed USB data rate?

more.text: 12 Mbit/s.
Devices publish messages to topics through a broker, and subscribers receive them. Low overhead for constrained devices.

sides.text: Which messaging pattern does MQTT use?

more.text: Publish/subscribe via a broker.
Lookup tables, flip-flops, and programmable routing implement any digital circuit. Massive parallelism and deterministic timing, but harder to design than software.

sides.text: What are an FPGA's basic building blocks?

more.text: Lookup tables, flip-flops, and programmable routing.
HDL code describes concurrent logic that gets synthesized into gates. Simulation and timing analysis come before hardware.

sides.text: Does HDL code run sequentially like C?

more.text: No. It describes concurrent hardware.
Occurs when an asynchronous input changes near the clock edge. A two-flip-flop synchronizer lets it settle before use.

sides.text: What circuit is used when crossing clock domains to reduce metastability?

more.text: A multi-stage flip-flop synchronizer.
The clock period must exceed the longest path delay plus setup time. Hold violations are fixed by adding delay.

sides.text: What must the clock period exceed?

more.text: The longest path delay plus setup time.

sides.text: A whole system on one die

more.text: CPU cores, memory controllers, GPU, and peripherals integrated together. Examples: Raspberry Pi's Broadcom chips, Apple's M-series, and Qualcomm Snapdragon.
A chip integrating CPU, memory controller, and peripherals into one system.

sides.text: Kernel, drivers, and a device tree

more.text: Describes hardware to the kernel through a device tree. PREEMPT_RT improves real-time behavior but is not a hard real-time guarantee on its own.

sides.text: What describes the hardware layout to the Linux kernel?

more.text: The device tree.

sides.text: Combine sensors for a better estimate

more.text: A complementary filter blends a gyroscope (fast, drifts) with an accelerometer (noisy, no drift) to estimate orientation. A Kalman filter generalizes this.

sides.text: Which sensor drifts over time, the gyroscope or the accelerometer?

more.text: The gyroscope.
The upper limit on error-free data rate for bandwidth B and linear SNR.

sides.text: B = 1 MHz and SNR = 31 (linear). What is the capacity?

more.text: 5 Mbit/s (log₂ 32 = 5).

sides.text: Energy per bit over noise density

more.text: BER falls as Eb/N0 rises. Coding trades extra bits for lower required Eb/N0 (coding gain). BPSK reaches 10⁻⁵ BER near 9.6 dB.
Reaching the same BER at a lower Eb/N0.
16-QAM sends 4 bits per symbol, 64-QAM sends 6. Denser constellations need higher SNR.

sides.text: How many bits per symbol does 64-QAM carry?
Avoid symbols smearing into each other

more.text: Raised-cosine filters satisfy the Nyquist criterion for zero intersymbol interference at the sampling instants.

sides.text: What does a raised-cosine filter help avoid?

more.text: Intersymbol interference.
Orthogonal subcarriers resist multipath. A cyclic prefix handles delay spread. Used in Wi-Fi, LTE, and 5G. Drawback: high peak-to-average power ratio.

sides.text: What does a cyclic prefix handle?

more.text: Multipath delay spread.

sides.text: Spread the signal over a wider band

more.text: DSSS multiplies by a fast code. FHSS hops frequencies. Gives interference resistance and low detectability. Processing gain = spread bandwidth / data bandwidth.

sides.text: What does DSSS multiply the data by?

more.text: A fast spreading code.
TDMA divides time, FDMA divides frequency, CDMA uses codes, and OFDMA assigns groups of subcarriers (used in Wi-Fi 6 and 5G).

sides.text: Which scheme assigns groups of OFDM subcarriers to users?

more.text: OFDMA.
Spatial multiplexing sends parallel streams, and diversity improves reliability. Capacity grows with min(Tx, Rx) antennas in a rich scattering environment.

sides.text: What does MIMO's spatial multiplexing do?

more.text: Sends several data streams in parallel over the same band.
Add structured redundancy to correct errors. LDPC and polar codes are used in 5G, with LDPC for data and polar for control.

sides.text: Which code does 5G use for control channels?

more.text: Polar codes.

Rayleigh fading has no line of sight
Rician has a dominant path. Flat fading affects all frequencies alike
frequency-selective fading varies across the band

sides.text: Which fading model has no line-of-sight path?

more.text: Rayleigh fading.
Zero-forcing inverts the channel but amplifies noise. MMSE balances distortion and noise.

sides.text: Which equalizer amplifies noise the most?

more.text: Zero-forcing.
Recover carrier frequency, phase, and symbol timing with preambles and PLLs.

sides.text: What do receivers recover to demodulate correctly?

more.text: Carrier phase and symbol timing.
Received power depends on antenna gains, wavelength, and distance in free space.

sides.text: Why does path loss rise with frequency for fixed-gain antennas?

more.text: Because λ shrinks, reducing the effective capture area.
Measured in dBi against an isotropic radiator. Higher gain means a narrower beam.

sides.text: What does a higher-gain antenna have?

more.text: A narrower beam.
The weakest signal a receiver can decode.

sides.text: B = 1 MHz, NF = 5 dB, and SNR_min = 10 dB. What is the sensitivity?

more.text: −99 dBm.

sides.text: How well an amplifier stays linear

more.text: P1dB is the input level where gain drops 1 dB. IP3 predicts third-order intermodulation products from two tones.
Third-order intermodulation distortion.
Superheterodyne mixes to an IF with strong filtering and has an image frequency problem. Direct conversion (zero-IF) is simpler, but has DC offset and I/Q imbalance.

sides.text: Which receiver mixes straight to baseband?

more.text: Direct conversion (zero-IF).
The output contains sum and difference frequencies. A filter picks the wanted one.

sides.text: What two frequencies does an ideal mixer produce?

more.text: The sum and difference of its inputs.
Wi-Fi 4 (n) added MIMO, Wi-Fi 5 (ac) wider channels, Wi-Fi 6 (ax) OFDMA and better efficiency, and Wi-Fi 7 (be) wider channels and multi-link operation.
Uses OFDM with scalable subcarrier spacing, bands from sub-GHz to mmWave, beamforming, and low-latency modes for critical services.

sides.text: Which technique focuses 5G energy toward users?

more.text: Beamforming (massive MIMO).
Peripherals advertise, a central connects, and data moves in short connection events described by GATT services and characteristics.

sides.text: What does a BLE peripheral do to be discovered?

more.text: Advertise.

sides.text: Chirp spread spectrum for long range

more.text: Trades data rate for sensitivity, reaching kilometers at very low power.

sides.text: What does LoRa trade for long range?

more.text: Data rate.
Loss is measured in dB/km. WDM sends several wavelengths on one fiber to multiply capacity.
Sends multiple wavelengths on one fiber.

sides.text: Distributed wiring matters when length > λ/10

more.text: Characteristic impedance Z₀ = √(L′/C′). A line terminated in Z₀ absorbs the wave without reflections.

sides.text: When does a wire need transmission-line treatment?

more.text: When its length is a significant fraction of the wavelength (about λ/10).
Zero for a perfect match, +1 for an open, and −1 for a short.

sides.text: Z₀ = 50 Ω and Z_L = 100 Ω. What is Γ?

more.text: A VSWR of 1 is a perfect match. Higher means more reflection.
Larger return loss means a better match.
20 dB.
Lets you see how a line or matching network moves an impedance. The center is a perfect match.

sides.text: What does the center of a Smith chart represent?

more.text: A perfect match (Z = Z₀).
Methods: L-networks, stubs, and a quarter-wave transformer with Z = √(Z₀ Z_L).

sides.text: Match 50 Ω to 200 Ω with a quarter-wave line. What impedance?
High-frequency current crowds at the surface

more.text: Skin depth falls as 1/√f, so resistance rises with frequency. Litz wire and plating help.

sides.text: Why does AC resistance rise with frequency?

more.text: Current is pushed to the conductor's surface (skin effect).

sides.text: A controlled-impedance PCB trace over a ground plane

more.text: Width, dielectric thickness, and εr set the impedance (often 50 Ω). Signals travel at roughly 60% of the speed of light on FR-4.
Trace width, dielectric thickness, and dielectric constant.
S11 is input reflection and S21 is forward transmission (gain). A vector network analyzer (VNA) measures them.
